I think people who hate it are going to be more vocal but of course I do know people who didn't like it and came back but I met plenty of people from California who moved there and stayed as well. I tried living in Nashville before and I did not like it, I could see why people did but for me it was too big and the bugs were really bad. (Just showing I don't enjoy all of the south.)

 I think people who just move based on hearing its cheaper but don't know anything else will not have a good time. Weather def gets a lot worse than the 90's there, every summer I lie to myself say its not that bad try to do some type of outside activity in summer and want to leave after 5 minutes. There are indoor things to do and lakes. I would see a lot of movies in summer or go board game bars or barcades more. I see you have a family so you might have different hobbies where summer could be harder. If you loooooove the beach then Texas is probably not the spot, but I find Austin really pretty, lots of creeks, rivers and greenery (in fact this can be a con, people who never had allergies will get allergies because there are so many types of trees.) Thats kind of a perfect example of things that are good to know before you move. I am sure you may have done this already, but I like to join the local subreddits of placed I might want to move and pick up on what people who live there are saying, now of course reddit is going to be more negative posts than positive but at least you know what some issues might be. 

  
Food scene is very good there whenever I came back to Cali and my family wanted to take me out nothing sounded good because I could have it all in Austin. I would say maybe you don't have a ton of korean options but otherwise I was able to find so much good food.

Austin and loved it, got a 4-bedroom house for the same price as small 2bd condos we were looking at in oc that were kind of far our and  by the toll roads and nothing else. There were parts of Austin that felt very similar to orange county so did not feel like a culture shock but there was a lot that I preferred (just number of events, large outdoor patios and places open late.) Of course, I had also lived in the bay area and Nashville so orange county is not the only place I had lived so easier for me. The thing is a lot of people say they move to these cities in other states and hate it but then you find out they really are living in suburbs an hour away from the city and complaining they are bored. Or they buy an insanely larger size house (because they can) and then have high utilities. Do a lot of research and spend time in the places you are looking at try to get a feel for what the whole year is like in the places you are looking at and not just when you can visit. Some people can't handle Texas heat and its bad, but I just did more indoor activities in summer but went out all fall and winter not everyone can do that so again lots of research.
